Core types ported from mholt/archives (archives.go + interfaces.go).

Go uses io/fs.FileInfo and io.Reader/Writer abstractions. In Nim we use our own io core (Input/Output over memfiles) and model file metadata explicitly.

io

  file*: FileInfo ## Result channel replacement: caller-supplied proc receiving the error
                  ## (nil as empty string means success).
  result*: proc (err: string) {.closure.}
ArchiveContext = object
  cancelled*: ptr bool
Minimal cancellation token replacing Go's context.Context. 
ArchiveError = object of CatchableError
FileHandler = proc (ctx: ArchiveContext; info: FileInfo) {.closure.}
Called for each entry while extracting/walking. Raise SkipDir to skip a directory, SkipAll to stop the walk. 
FileInfo = object
  meta*: FileMeta ## The file header as used/provided by the archive format.
                  ## Kept as a string dump or format-specific ref; nil when creating.
  header*: RootRef           ## Path of the file as it appears in the archive (slash separated).
  nameInArchive*: string     ## For symbolic and hard links, the target of the link.
  linkTarget*: string ## Opens the file content for reading. Zero-copy when the entry is
                      ## backed by mapped memory: no read syscalls, no buffer copies.
  open*: proc (): Input {.closure.}
A virtualized file abstraction for interacting with archives. Port of Go's archives.FileInfo. 
FileMeta = object
  name*: string              ## base name (not full archive path)
  size*: int64
  mode*: int                 ## raw Unix mode bits (permissions + file type)
  modTime*: Time
  isDir*: bool
  isSymlink*: bool
  isRegular*: bool
Virtualized file metadata, replaces fs.FileInfo. 
FileMode = distinct int
Minimal mode bits. We preserve Unix permission bits plus dir/symlink markers; mirrors the subset of fs.FileMode we need.

proc stringOpener(data: string): proc (): Input {.closure.} {....raises: [],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Factory returning an opener closure over its own copy of data. Must be used instead of inline closures in loops: Nim closures created in a loop body share the captured variable slot, so an inline opener would serve the LAST file's data to every entry. A proc parameter is fresh per call. Zero-copy: the string is shared by reference, never copied.

Opener over a borrowed span (e.g. an entry inside a mapped archive). keep retains the parent mapping/string.
